creator: Rooke Poole
scope: Closure of the 29 findings in the v0.3.6 comprehensive bug audit.
environment_note: All automated tests were run in Linux. Windows picker process/PowerShell contracts are automated; physical Windows dialog acceptance is supplied as a manual release gate.

findings.audit_title: Snapshot restore deletes the live workspace before validating recovery objects
findings.resolution: Restore now validates every required object before workspace mutation, stages the target tree, and rolls back on failure.
findings.original_impact: A missing snapshot object causes restore to fail after current files have already been deleted. The working tree can be destroyed or left partially restored.
findings.original_recommendation: Preflight every manifest entry, verify object hashes and free space, restore into a staging directory, then atomically swap or roll back.

findings.audit_title: Corrupted content-addressed snapshot objects are restored without hash verification
findings.resolution: Restore, export, Doctor, and safety paths recompute SHA-256 and reject object/manifest mismatches.
findings.original_impact: A damaged or tampered object is trusted based only on its filename. Restore can silently write corrupted content while reporting success.
findings.original_recommendation: Recompute SHA-256 for every object during Doctor, restore, export, and merge safety checks; reject mismatches before touching the workspace.

findings.audit_title: Repository locks work only inside one Python process
findings.closure_title: Cross-process locking and unique state writes
findings.resolution: Repository UUID/path locks and an application-data single-instance lock serialize writers across processes; state writes use unique atomic temporary files.
findings.original_impact: Two ForgeTrace instances or processes editing the same repository race on the fixed state.json.tmp file. Three runs lost 35-37 operations; one run also lost a repository file.
findings.original_recommendation: Add an operating-system file lock keyed by repository UUID/path, unique temporary filenames, optimistic revision checks, and a single-instance lock for shared app data.

findings.audit_title: Repository paths are sorted globally by depth instead of parent-child order
findings.resolution: Repository state is emitted in parent-child order with depth/parent metadata; the browser renders a true nested virtualized tree.
findings.original_impact: Expanding a folder does not place its children beneath it. The reproduced UI order was Alpha, Beta, root.txt, Alpha/inside. This is the strongest confirmed explanation for users believing subfolder files did not populate.
findings.original_recommendation: Return a nested tree or stable depth-first order. Render children recursively inside their parent node rather than filtering a flat globally sorted list.

findings.audit_title: Direct folder import silently overwrites existing files
findings.resolution: Imports preview conflicts and require abort, skip, overwrite, or rename behavior. Overwrite creates recovery state.
findings.original_impact: Existing repository content can be replaced with no conflict preview, confirmation, safety snapshot, or rollback point.
findings.original_recommendation: Add explicit conflict policies (abort, skip, overwrite, rename), default to abort, show a preview, and create a safety snapshot before any overwrite.

findings.audit_title: Folder import is non-transactional and leaves partial untracked files on failure
findings.resolution: Folder imports stage outside the live workspace, verify bytes, commit transactionally, and leave no partial untracked tree on failure/cancel.
findings.original_impact: Earlier files remain copied when a later conflict/error aborts the import, but no contribution is recorded. Repository contents and ForgeTrace history diverge.
findings.original_recommendation: Stage the full import outside the repository, validate all conflicts first, then apply atomically with rollback and one metadata transaction.

findings.audit_title: New-repository folder import is split across two requests and can leave an orphan repository
findings.resolution: New repository creation and folder population are one registry operation; failed imports remove staging and registration artifacts.
findings.original_impact: ForgeTrace registers and activates a managed repository before import. If import fails, a README-only repository remains in the list and can look like the selected folder was empty.
findings.original_recommendation: Create-and-import in one server transaction or automatically unregister/delete the new managed repository after a failed import, with a clear recovery prompt.

findings.audit_title: Filesystem mutations can succeed even when contribution metadata fails to save
findings.resolution: File changes and state updates share rollback journals; metadata-save failure restores the prior filesystem state.
findings.original_impact: A file write can survive while the API returns an error and contribution history remains unchanged. Similar ordering exists in rename, delete, import, and other operations.
findings.original_recommendation: Use a write-ahead operation journal or transaction directory, save an intent/revision first, then commit filesystem and metadata together with rollback.

findings.audit_title: state.json.bak is created and detected but cannot be restored by Doctor
findings.resolution: Doctor validates state.json.bak, restores it atomically, preserves a repair backup, and verifies repository UUID/schema.
findings.original_impact: A repository can become unusable after state.json corruption even though a valid backup is present and Doctor reports backupAvailable=true.
findings.original_recommendation: Add previewed backup validation, one-click restore, automatic pre-repair backup, schema/UUID checks, and rollback if recovery fails.

findings.audit_title: Nested .forgetrace metadata is imported into repositories
findings.resolution: Import policy rejects .forgetrace at any path depth instead of excluding only the selected root.
findings.original_impact: Only a root-level .forgetrace directory is excluded. Nested project histories and object stores can be copied, exposed in the UI/export, and greatly inflate imports.
findings.original_recommendation: Reject any path segment named .forgetrace at every depth and report each excluded path.

findings.audit_title: A stale directory at the old path prevents UUID-based startup relinking
findings.resolution: Startup discovery compares embedded identities even when the old path still exists with a stale/wrong identity.
findings.original_impact: After moving a repository, an empty/stale old directory causes ForgeTrace to retain an uninitialized record even though the real UUID-bearing repository is discovered elsewhere.
findings.original_recommendation: Treat path identity, not path existence, as authoritative. Relink when the old path lacks the expected UUID and exactly one discovered candidate matches.

findings.audit_title: A localStorage failure after successful copy is reported as an import failure
findings.resolution: UI persistence failures fall back to in-memory expansion and cannot convert a successful disk import into a failed result.
validation_evidence: index.html: expandedMemory and import completion flow
findings.original_impact: The server can copy every file successfully, then UI expansion-state persistence throws. ForgeTrace displays “Native folder import failed,” skips refresh, and makes successful files appear absent.
findings.original_recommendation: Make expansion-state persistence best-effort and isolated from import success. Always refresh server state after copy, then warn separately if UI preferences could not be saved.

findings.audit_title: Every state refresh repeatedly walks and hashes the entire repository
findings.resolution: A repository-local cache reuses size/mtime/hash metadata for unchanged files and avoids rehashing the full tree on every refresh.
findings.original_impact: api_state calls tree multiple times and hashes every file to compute dirty state. Measured API state time was ~0.87 s at 10,000 tiny files before network/DOM cost; real binaries and slower drives can make imports look stuck or incomplete.
findings.original_recommendation: Add an indexed manifest with incremental filesystem changes, cache hashes by size/mtime/file ID, and expose scan progress/cancellation.

findings.audit_title: Folder rename and delete controls are disabled
findings.resolution: Folder actions are available in the UI and execute through transactional repository APIs.
findings.original_impact: Selecting a folder clears selectedFile, which disables rename/delete along with file-only actions, despite backend support for folder rename/delete.
findings.original_recommendation: Track a selected tree entry separately from selected file content; enable rename/delete for both files and folders.

findings.audit_title: Import verification checks path existence, not byte size or content hash
findings.resolution: Import manifests verify path, type, size, and SHA-256, not existence alone.
findings.original_impact: Truncated, changed, or wrong file contents can pass verification as long as the expected path exists.
findings.original_recommendation: Capture source size/hash during enumeration and verify destination content before reporting success.

findings.audit_title: No total import-size or destination free-space preflight
findings.resolution: Imports calculate total bytes and compare required staging/commit space with destination free space before mutation.
findings.original_impact: Only individual file limits are checked. A large tree can exhaust disk space midway and trigger the partial-import defect.
findings.original_recommendation: Sum bytes before copying, compare with free space plus safety margin, enforce configurable total limits, and fail before creating destination files.

findings.audit_title: Direct import enumerates the complete tree in memory with no progress or cancellation
findings.resolution: Long imports run as persistent jobs with bounded history, progress counters, cancellation, and interrupted-job recovery.
findings.original_impact: Large or network folders can block one request for minutes. The UI cannot show discovery/copy progress or cancel safely.
findings.original_recommendation: Use a job model with phases, counters, cancellation tokens, resumable staging, and a persistent operation log.

findings.audit_title: Snapshots do not preserve empty directories
findings.resolution: Snapshot manifests record directories and restore empty directory structure.
findings.original_impact: Restoring a snapshot can produce a structurally different project even when no file content is missing.
findings.original_recommendation: Include directory manifests and restore empty directories explicitly.

findings.audit_title: Snapshots do not preserve permissions, executable bits, timestamps, or other metadata
findings.resolution: Snapshot/restore preserves supported mode bits and nanosecond modification timestamps.
findings.original_impact: Restored scripts/build assets may lose executable or metadata semantics, especially on macOS/Linux.
findings.original_recommendation: Store documented portable metadata and restore it where supported, with clear cross-platform fallbacks.

findings.audit_title: Repository export is not protected by the repository mutation lock
findings.resolution: Export acquires the repository mutation lock and streams from verified snapshot/object content.
findings.original_impact: Files can be renamed/deleted while an archive is being built, causing inconsistent archives or failures.
findings.original_recommendation: Create a stable manifest/snapshot under lock and export from immutable objects or a staging view.

findings.audit_title: Closed/merged pull-request quarantine cleanup exists but is never invoked
findings.resolution: Merged/closed request quarantine is purged immediately and terminal/stale data is cleaned on collaboration startup.
findings.original_impact: Submitted files can remain indefinitely in application data, consuming disk and retaining content users may assume was removed.
findings.original_recommendation: Add retention policy, owner-visible storage metrics, purge after merge/close, and safe scheduled cleanup.

findings.audit_title: Crash leftovers in transfers and merge-backups have no startup cleanup/recovery policy
findings.resolution: Pending filesystem transactions recover on repository open; stale transfer, merge-backup, and unregistered staging artifacts are bounded/cleaned.
findings.original_impact: Interrupted forks, downloads, or merges can leave large temporary data or ambiguous rollback directories.
findings.original_recommendation: Record transfer/merge leases, clean expired safe artifacts at startup, and surface recoverable interrupted operations.

findings.audit_title: Import/share/export workflows lack a sensitive-file preview
findings.resolution: Import/share/export surfaces classify sensitive paths, exclude them by default where appropriate, and require explicit confirmation.
findings.original_impact: Hidden files, .env files, credentials, build caches, and VCS data can be imported/exported unless a specific source-only path excludes some metadata.
findings.original_recommendation: Add ignore rules, secret-name warnings, size previews, and a share/export manifest requiring explicit approval.

findings.audit_title: Browser tests inject mocked transport instead of exercising the packaged server
findings.closure_title: Real server + real disk browser test
findings.resolution: A black-box browser flow uses the actual packaged UI, HTTP handler, repository service, and filesystem; mocked UI tests remain supplemental.
findings.original_impact: Tests can pass while real routing, filesystem behavior, Windows picker behavior, serialization, or state refresh is broken. This produced false confidence around the recurring folder issue.
findings.original_recommendation: Add true black-box tests that launch the packaged server, operate through real HTTP, inspect real disk output, and run on Windows CI.

findings.audit_title: Native folder picker has only 23% unit coverage and no real Windows chooser test
findings.closure_title: Picker adapter coverage and Windows acceptance harness
findings.resolution: Platform adapters, PowerShell 7/Windows PowerShell STA invocation, Unicode, cancel, and headless contracts are automated. A dedicated Windows physical-dialog acceptance script/checklist is included.
findings.original_impact: The primary Windows workflow depends on PowerShell/WinForms but is tested through an environment override or mocked API, not the actual user interaction.
findings.original_recommendation: Run Windows 10/11 CI or a manual acceptance harness for PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7, Unicode paths, network drives, cancellation, hidden windows, and long paths.

findings.audit_title: The file tree renders all visible rows with no virtualization
findings.resolution: The browser renders a bounded visible window with spacer rows instead of inserting all expanded paths into the DOM.
findings.original_impact: 100,000 rows generated ~23.3 MB of HTML and took ~1.34 s just to assign innerHTML in headless Chromium. Auto-expanding imported trees magnifies memory and responsiveness problems.
findings.original_recommendation: Use a real nested virtualized tree, lazy child loading, row recycling, and bounded expansion.

findings.audit_title: HTTP server lacks explicit request/socket timeouts and does not implement HEAD
findings.resolution: Threaded servers have socket timeouts/backlog limits and implement HEAD for health/static/API paths.
findings.original_impact: Slow clients can occupy threads longer than necessary; standard health/proxy HEAD checks receive 501.
findings.original_recommendation: Set connection/read timeouts, body deadlines, bounded thread behavior, and implement HEAD for static/version health resources.

findings.audit_title: Remote rate-limit client maps can retain inactive keys
findings.resolution: Inactive rate buckets are pruned and the map is capped to prevent unbounded key retention.
findings.original_impact: Long-running gateways can accumulate small amounts of per-client bookkeeping.
findings.original_recommendation: Evict expired/empty keys periodically and cap map size.

findings.audit_title: Core routing and import functions are highly monolithic
findings.resolution: Monolithic request/import logic was split into scoped dispatchers and services with AST complexity/length guards.
findings.original_impact: Large branch-heavy functions increase regression risk and make route-level security/transaction review difficult.
findings.original_recommendation: Split handlers into typed route controllers/services, isolate transaction stages, and enforce complexity thresholds in CI.
